annotation.title_clean: Encoding the Enforcement of Safety Standards into Smart Robots to Harness Their Computing Sophistication and Collaborative Potential: A Legal Risk Assessment for European Union Policymakers
annotation.title_en: Encoding the Enforcement of Safety Standards into Smart Robots to Harness Their Computing Sophistication and Collaborative Potential: A Legal Risk Assessment for European Union Policymakers
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed legal analysis of occupational health and safety rules for smart collaborative robots in the EU. It finds gaps in current standards, the Machinery Regulation and the draft AI Act and AI Liability Directive. It proposes encoding OHS enforcement into the robots themselves, using quantum computing, and a new binding EU OHS Regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Current EU directives, standards and the 2023 Machinery Regulation inadequately address physical and mental risks of smart cobots.
Proposes encoding OHS rule enforcement directly into smart cobots, possibly using quantum computing.
Calls for a new binding EU OHS Regulation uniting robotics safety and AI frameworks.
Raises open questions on robot legal personality, liability apportionment and explainability.
Highlights the AI Liability Directive's burden-of-proof relief for harm caused by opaque AI.
